VIF-A advertises:
- 10.10.0.0/24 → covers 10.10.0.0 – 10.10.0.255
- 10.10.1.0/24 → covers 10.10.1.0 – 10.10.1.255
- 10.10.2.0/23 → covers 10.10.2.0 – 10.10.3.255 (this spans both the 10.10.2.0/24 and 10.10.3.0/24 ranges)

Adding those up: 0.0/24 + 1.0/24 + 2.0/23 (which absorbs 2.0/24 and 3.0/24) = the full 10.10.0.0 – 10.10.3.255 range.

**Yes — the /22 is fully protected if VIF-B fails.** VIF-A's three advertised prefixes collectively cover the entire 10.10.0.0/22 range with no gaps:

| Range | Covered by VIF-A? |
|---|---|
| 10.10.0.0/24 | ✅ direct match |
| 10.10.1.0/24 | ✅ direct match |
| 10.10.2.0/24 | ✅ within 10.10.2.0/23 |
| 10.10.3.0/24 | ✅ within 10.10.2.0/23 |

One caveat worth flagging: this is a route-coverage check based on the prefixes you gave me — it confirms VIF-A *advertises* overlapping routes, not that the failover actually works in practice (BGP convergence time, whether VIF-A terminates on a diverse Direct Connect location/device, LAG health, etc.).
